description:
What was sprayed, where, when, by whom, in what weather. This is the EVENT; Spray Tank Mix is the recipe. It is the record a state pesticide inspector asks for by name, and the shape of it is that question: product and rate, block and acres, applicator and licence, start and finish, and the wind and temperature at the time — which is the half most farms keep on a clipboard and lose.

THE MIX IS COPIED ONTO THE APPLICATION, NOT JUST LINKED. `products_applied` holds the mix as it stood when the tank was loaded. A mix somebody re-rates in July does not retroactively change what went out in May, and a record that read its rates through a live link would claim exactly that.

IT OPENS RESTRICTED ENTRY AND DOES NOT REPLACE IT. One Spray REI record per block, because 'is block 7 clear' has to be one indexed query at a gate rather than a scan of the application register. This record is where the window came from; Spray REI is what answers for it.

WEATHER IS RECORDED, NOT ENFORCED. Wind outside the label's window and a temperature inversion are advisories on the record rather than refusals. A spray that happened is a fact, and an app that refuses to record it because the wind was 12 mph has not prevented the spray — it has only prevented the record of it, which is the outcome an inspector cares about most and the operator least.

fields.description: Applied is a spray that happened. Planned is one scheduled and not yet made — it opens no restricted entry, because nothing has been put on the ground. Cancelled is a record withdrawn, kept rather than deleted for the same reason a cancelled REI is: a restriction published to a crew and then lifted is itself something an inspector may ask about.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: The recipe this tank was loaded from. Optional: a spray mixed at the machine with no recipe on file is still a spray, and refusing to record it would push it onto a clipboard.
fields.label: Tank Mix

fields.description: The applicator's licence or certification number as the state issued it. On the record rather than looked up, because the question is always 'who was licensed on that day' and a licence that has since lapsed still licensed this pass.
fields.label: Applicator Licence

fields.description: The Farm Task this spray closed, where it came off one. Empty is legitimate — somebody mixed a tank and drove.
fields.label: Source Task

fields.description: When the application FINISHED. Every restricted-entry window runs from here (or from a block's own completion, where the pass was long enough for them to differ) and not from when this was filed, so a record entered the next morning does not shut a block for an extra night.
fields.label: Completed At

fields.description: Ground speed driven. With the nozzle set's flow and spacing this is what gives gallons per acre — the calibration figure, which is the one an inspector recomputes rather than reads.
fields.label: Ground Speed (mph)

fields.description: Every block this pass reached, with the acres covered on each.
fields.label: Blocks

fields.description: Sum of the block acres, rewritten on every save.
fields.label: Total Acres

fields.description: The tank mix AS IT STOOD when this tank was loaded, as JSON — [{item_code, item_name, rate_per_acre, rate_uom, nozzle_set, rei_hours, phi_days, epa_reg_number, total_applied}]. Copied rather than read through the link, because a mix re-rated in July did not change what went out in May.
fields.label: Products Applied

fields.description: The flip actually happened during this pass. A dual-set machine driven without flipping put only one set's products on the ground, and that is the difference between what was planned and what was applied.
fields.label: Flip Performed

fields.description: Gallons of finished spray per acre, computed from the nozzle set's flow rate, its spacing and the ground speed where all three are known. Read-only: it is the calibration arithmetic, and a typed figure is one nobody can check.
fields.label: Gallons / Acre

fields.description: Wind speed at the time of application. Most labels set a window — commonly 3 to 10 mph — and both ends matter: above it is drift, below it is a temperature inversion that holds the spray in a layer and moves it somewhere nobody chose.
fields.label: Wind Speed (mph)

fields.description: Direction the wind was FROM, in the compass words a person says — 'WSW'. Free text rather than degrees, because it is written by somebody standing in a block with a hand meter.
fields.label: Wind From

fields.description: Where the reading came from. An inspector treats a hand meter at the block and a station eight miles away differently, and a record that does not say which has made that judgement for them.
fields.label: Weather Source
fields.options:
Observed
On-Site Station
Nearby Station
Forecast API
Estimated

fields.description: When the reading was taken. A reading from three hours before the pass is a different fact from one taken at the block, and the gap is what says which.
fields.label: Weather Recorded At

fields.description: What was outside the ordinary window at application time — wind too high, wind low enough for an inversion, temperature high enough for volatilisation, weather not recorded at all. Written on every save. ADVISORY, NOT A REFUSAL: a spray that happened is a fact, and refusing the record does not undo the pass.
fields.label: Weather Advisories

fields.description: The longest restricted-entry interval in the tank. What actually shut the blocks.
fields.label: REI Hours

fields.description: When the LAST block of this application clears. Per-block expiry is on each Spray REI record, which is what a gate asks.
fields.label: REI Expires At

fields.description: The earliest date this fruit may be harvested. The number that decides whether a block can be picked, which is why it is stored rather than recomputed off a master somebody may correct.
fields.label: PHI Clears On

fields.description: How many Spray REI windows this application opened. Zero on a Planned application, and zero where nothing in the tank has a label interval — which is the ordinary case for a foliar nutrient and is different from a failure.
fields.label: REI Records Created

name: Spray Application
